title: The Data engineer in the built chat: what is missing, a new column from a formula, a lookup join, each in a new version only
request: Data agent: "add this column", "join this table", "what's missing in the data", from the built chat.
spec: The built chat's version flow (propose, confirm, plan, build: a new project, the built one unchanged); dclab_core.datacard (bands, never a row); dclab_core.meet.
plan: studio/derive.py: formulas parsed against a whitelist, never run; lookup joins only; a version's changes applied in order.
data_gaps from the data card and meet.check; propose_data_change and confirm_data_change; plan and build apply data_ops to the version's copy.
Review; fix; tests for every finding.

decisions.decision: Every data change goes into a new version; the built project's table never changes.
decisions.why: A new column can leak; the new version runs the leakage audit and every stage again, and reads its holdout once.

decisions.decision: Only lookup joins (the key unique in the other table).
decisions.why: An event table needs its rows summed up to the prediction moment with a time cutoff, or it leaks what happened after.

decisions.decision: Formulas are parsed with ast against a whitelist.
decisions.why: A person's or a model's formula must never run code.

change: dclab_rnd/studio/derive.py (new), dclab_rnd/draft/orchestrator.py (Data engineer, data_gaps, propose/confirm_data_change, data_ops in plan and build), tests/test_studio_derive.py, tests/test_home_orchestrator.py

findings.defect: A new column could be built from a later version's outcome.
findings.scenario: Outcome changed to churned_60d, then add column leak = churned_60d + spend / 60: accepted, AUC 0.87 in the built table.
findings.cause: The check read version 1's outcome and forbidden list only.
findings.fix: _never_from: every version's outcome and plan-forbidden columns; a problem change drops data changes that read its outcome, and says so.

findings.defect: A join's key was never checked.
findings.scenario: join labels on churned, where the other table maps churned to a status.
findings.cause: check_join checked the joined columns, not the key.
findings.fix: The key goes through blocked_inputs (outcomes, forbidden, suspects).

findings.defect: A joined table that changed after confirmation was joined whole.
findings.scenario: The other table gains a churned column before the build.
findings.cause: apply re-read the source and took every column.
findings.fix: The op keeps the checked columns and a content fingerprint; apply refuses a changed table.

findings.defect: A renamed joined column could overwrite an existing column, the outcome included.
findings.scenario: Frame has churn and the outcome plans_churn; plans has churn.
findings.cause: The rename to table_column did not check the new name.
findings.fix: Refused when the new name exists; apply uses the checked names.

findings.defect: After a version was built, the next lost the earlier changes.
findings.scenario: Outcome version built, then add column: version 3 went back to churned.
findings.fix: _last_version (built or not) for the problem and the data changes.

findings.defect: is_missing and the date functions read text columns as numbers.
findings.scenario: is_missing(plan) gave 1 on every row; month(day) on text dates gave nothing.
findings.cause: Every column was turned into numbers first.
findings.fix: Those functions read the column as it is.

findings.defect: Plot and other requests were routed to the Data engineer.
findings.scenario: "add a column chart", "join us", "what's the null hypothesis?".
findings.cause: Wide patterns ran before PLOT and the reads.
findings.fix: NOT_DATA, FORMULA_LIKE, a table word for joins, a data word for nulls.

findings.defect: A numpy refusal reached the person as "the table cannot be read".
findings.cause: Only ChangeRefused was said as such.
findings.fix: compute turns any other error into ChangeRefused.

measurements.name: affected tests
measurements.result: home orchestrator 62, derive 5, data limits 36, journeys built 6
limits: no live model run of the Data engineer yet

outcome: The chat's Data engineer says what is missing, and adds columns or lookup tables only through a new version that is audited again.
lessons: A leakage check must read every outcome in play, not the one the project was built for.
Whatever is re-read at build time must be the thing that was checked: keep a fingerprint.
risks: Event tables (one-to-many) are refused rather than aggregated at the prediction moment.
